Scheduling & dispatch tools for Electricians

Tools that help electricians with scheduling & dispatch. Booking jobs, routing crews, managing calendars and reducing no-shows.

Where Scheduling & dispatch goes wrong for Electricians

Electrical work is dictated by the other trades on site — first fix cannot happen before the plasterer, second fix cannot happen after them. Schedules slip for reasons outside your control.

What Electricians jobs really involve

Electrical work carries certification and documentation duties that most other trades do not, so paperwork is genuinely part of the job rather than an optional extra. Records of what was installed and tested matter long after the invoice is paid.

Frequently asked questions

Which scheduling & dispatch tools work best for electricians?

The three that fit best here are Housecall Pro (Home service businesses that want one app covering booking through to payment), Jobber (Owner-operators and small crews moving off paper and spreadsheets), ServiceTitan (Established businesses with multiple crews and a dedicated office team). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does scheduling & dispatch software cost for electricians?

Across the 6 tools on this page, 1 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does scheduling & dispatch cause problems for electricians specifically?

Electrical work is dictated by the other trades on site — first fix cannot happen before the plasterer, second fix cannot happen after them. Schedules slip for reasons outside your control.

Do I need software that stores electrical certificates?

Any system that lets you attach test results and certificates to a job and find them again later is enough. Dedicated certification apps only start to matter when you are issuing a large number of certificates every month.
